standards.title: Pass cancellation tokens through async operations
standards.guidance: When a method accepts a CancellationToken, pass it to downstream asynchronous operations that support cancellation.

standards.title: Avoid blocking asynchronous code
standards.guidance: Do not use .Result or .Wait() to synchronously block on a Task in application code; use await instead.

standards.title: Dispose owned disposable resources
standards.guidance: Dispose or asynchronously dispose resources your code creates and owns, using using or await using where appropriate.

standards.title: Do not use async void for ordinary methods
standards.guidance: Use async Task or async Task<T> for asynchronous methods. Reserve async void for event handlers that require it.

standards.title: Do not silently swallow exceptions
standards.guidance: Catch an exception only when the code can handle it, add useful context, or rethrow it. Do not leave catch blocks empty.

standards.title: Validate untrusted input at system boundaries
standards.guidance: Validate input from users, external services, and files before relying on its format, range, or required values.

standards.title: Authorize access to protected resources
standards.guidance: Before returning or modifying a protected resource, verify that the current caller is authorized for that resource.

standards.title: Use parameterized database queries
standards.guidance: Pass data values as query parameters rather than concatenating or interpolating them into SQL statements.

standards.title: Keep secrets out of source code
standards.guidance: Load credentials and API keys from an approved secret store or protected configuration; do not hard-code them.

standards.title: Avoid logging sensitive data
standards.guidance: Do not write passwords, access tokens, or other sensitive personal or organizational data to logs.

standards.title: Handle nullable values explicitly
standards.guidance: Check potentially absent values before dereferencing them, or use appropriate nullable types and flow checks.

standards.title: Avoid mutable shared state
standards.guidance: Do not share mutable state across requests or concurrent operations unless access is safely synchronized.

standards.title: Use specific exception types
standards.guidance: Throw an exception that describes the failure rather than using a general Exception for expected validation or state errors.

standards.title: Keep retry behavior bounded
standards.guidance: Retries for transient failures should have a defined limit and should not repeat non-idempotent operations unsafely.

standards.title: Test important behavior changes
standards.guidance: Add or update automated tests for changed behavior, especially error handling and important boundary cases.

standards.title: Avoid unexplained literal values
standards.guidance: Replace non-obvious repeated literal values with named constants or configuration values where that improves clarity.

standards.title: Keep methods focused
standards.guidance: Prefer methods with one clear responsibility; extract cohesive steps when a method becomes difficult to understand or test.

standards.title: Preserve public API compatibility
standards.guidance: Before changing a public method, type, or contract, check its callers and avoid breaking compatibility without an intentional migration.

standards.title: Use structured logging
standards.guidance: Prefer structured logging fields over building log messages through string concatenation or interpolation.

standards.title: Make collection ownership clear
standards.guidance: Avoid exposing mutable internal collections directly; return read-only views or copies when callers should not mutate internal state.
